title: Speaking, dictation and sounds
summary: Cards where the learner speaks or writes what was said, and pairs of sounds an English ear runs together.
description: Training for the ear and the mouth, which reading and tapping do not give. Sound pairs are real words that differ in one sound (sz and ś, y and i, ł and l).

stories.as: a learner who cannot yet tell similar Polish sounds apart
stories.want: to hear them side by side and be told which I confuse
stories.soThat: my ear and my pronunciation improve

stories.as: a learner speaking into the app
stories.want: my recordings not to be kept
stories.soThat: I can practise aloud without a record of it

requirements.text: A dictation answer is compared word by word: right words, wrong ones with the right form, words left out, and words that were not said.
In dictation a Polish letter typed without its mark is accepted, and pointed out.
A spoken answer is written down by the model chosen as Hearing you speak and compared word by word as a dictation is.
When a spoken word is heard as another that differs by a known sound contrast, the card says which sound and what to try.
Recordings are never stored or synced: they are passed to the model and dropped.
A recording is refused when it is larger than 4 MB once encoded as text, about 3 MB of audio.
Speaking cards take the place of a lesson's usual practice cards and do not add to its length.
Whether speaking cards are shown is a setting of the device, not of the learner.
A words lesson has a round of up to two sound pairs before its closing memory round, when its words have the sounds.
The built-in sound pairs ship with the app; nothing is written to the database for them.
